hypothesis_front.title: Discrete Condition on a Continuous Path
hypothesis_front.primary_statement: A continuous process can resolve discretely because continuity belongs to the path, while discreteness belongs to a distinguishable, bounded, or indexed condition on that path.
hypothesis_front.strong_form_candidate: A continuous process resolves discretely when a receiving relation maps a continuous family of trajectories into mutually exclusive closure classes and continuation leaves one class admissible.
hypothesis_front.author_correction: A discrete condition on a continuous path.
hypothesis_front.left_field_extension: Quantization may belong to classification of a process rather than to the process as substance; a quantum may be a discrete admissibility condition recurrently realized on a continuous relational path.
hypothesis_front.scope: General structural hypothesis first; quantum measurement is a temporary candidate application, not an established physical conclusion.

author_literal_record: A continuous process can resolve discretely because continuity belongs to the path, while discreteness belongs to the set of admissible closures.
The process does not need to jump.
i would have said a discrete condition on a continuious path
The path does not become discrete. The condition is discrete because it is distinguishable, bounded, or indexed at some ordinal location along that path.
a particle is a discrete distinction condition propagating along, or realized upon, a continuous field path
star here and hit one to left field what do we find?
A quantum is not necessarily a discrete piece of reality.
It may be a discrete admissibility condition recurrently realized on a continuous relational path.
That would relocate quantization from the ontology of substance to the topology of admissible distinction.
The path continues. The condition closes. The closure receives an index. What propagates is the distinction; what becomes discrete is its admissible identity.

continuous_path_model.meaning: Γ is a continuously traceable path through continuous possibility space X over ordinal continuation parameter Λ.
continuous_path_model.simultaneity: Γ is continuous while C_i is discrete relative to observation or closure.
continuous_path_model.continuation: C_i → C_{i+1} may remain relationally traceable even when C_i ≠ C_{i+1}.

closure_partition_model.outcome_map: O_x: X → {1,2,...,n}, O_x(z)=i iff z closes within B_i
closure_partition_model.discrete_resolution_condition: Alternative outcome continuations become inadmissible while the underlying path remains continuous.

quotient_model.interpretation: Discrete outcome is a discrete equivalence class with respect to the outcome criterion, not necessarily a discontinuous underlying process.

evaluator_model.interpretation: A continuous path may yield a discrete index sequence because the receiving evaluator supplies bounded admissibility classes.
evaluator_model.jump_reframe: A reported index may change i→j while continuity of Γ is not thereby disproved.
evaluator_model.recurrence: q_x(Γ(λ_1)) = q_x(Γ(λ_2)) = q_x(Γ(λ_3)) = i may represent recurrence of one distinction signature rather than transport of a substance.

rt_candidates.compact_principle: Continuity is a condition of continuation; discreteness is a condition of distinction.

measurement_framing.temporary_model: A continuously evolving relation interacts with a receiving apparatus whose stable pointer conditions form a bounded family of records.
measurement_framing.detector_partition: A_D = {D_+,D_-} or a finite indexed family.
measurement_framing.guardrail: Decoherence, detector dynamics, and individual-outcome selection remain separate physical questions; this packet does not claim to solve the measurement problem.

left_field_hypothesis.statement: Quantization may be a property of admissible classification and closure rather than a primitive discontinuity of the underlying process.
left_field_hypothesis.particle_reframe: A particle-like identity may be a recurrent discrete distinction condition on a continuous relational path.
excluded: quantization has been reduced to classification
particles are proven not to be substances

continuity_discreteness_relation.discreteness: Distinguishability, bounded closure, or indexing of a condition.
continuity_discreteness_relation.compatibility: The two predicates can hold simultaneously when they are typed to different aspects of the same relational process.
continuity_discreteness_relation.failure_condition: A fully typed same-path/same-condition case may still falsify the compatibility claim if no admissibility or evaluation distinction is available.

open_formal_obligations.title: Type continuous path space X and continuation Λ
Define bounded closure basins B_i and disjointness
Define Cl_x necessary and sufficient closure conditions
Type q_x and discrete index set I
Define quotient equivalence ~_x and preserve path information limits
Separate continuity of Γ from continuity/discontinuity of q_x∘Γ
Define recurrent identity condition and distinguish recurrence from transport
Map detector architecture to admissibility without physical overclaim
Relate Cl_x(C,B_i) to existing RT core without substitution
State falsification cases for discrete-condition/continuous-path compatibility

candidate_tests.criterion: Construct continuous Γ and finite q_x with at least two closure indices and no path discontinuity.
Verify Adm_x cardinality decreases to one only under declared boundary constraints.
Show distinct continuous histories map to one closure class while recording information loss.
Change q_x∘Γ from i to j while retaining a continuous Γ and identify conditions for admissibility.
Test repeated q_x(Γ)=i and distinguish recurrence of signature from persistent object transport.
Model a finite detector basin family and separate interaction, amplification, record formation, and outcome selection.

explicit_exclusions: No claim that underlying quantum processes are continuous in the physical sense.
No claim that all discrete outcomes are detector-created classifications.
No claim that q_x is lossless or invertible.
No claim that a particle is not a physical entity.
No claim that decoherence alone selects one individual outcome.
No completed QM-GR bridge or physical theory.
No replacement of the established RT core by the candidate forms.

canonical_summary.one_line: Γ may remain continuous while q_x(Γ) is discrete because continuity belongs to continuation and discreteness belongs to the indexed closure condition.
canonical_summary.compact_form: Γ:Λ→X; q_x:X→I; Γ continuous ∧ q_x∘Γ discrete; Resolve_x(C)=i iff Adm_x(C)={B_i}.
canonical_summary.guardrail: The left-field quantization framing is a speculative structural extension and remains separate from physical claims.
